newsitem.title: GERMANY: German economy still in uptrend - Econ Ministry.
newsitem.headline: German economy still in uptrend - Econ Ministry.

text.p: The German economy remains in an uptrend, the Economics Ministry said on Thursday, adding it sees no reason to change its forecast of 2.5 percent economic growth in 1997.

The ministry also said the recent strength of the dollar and seasonal factors in international commodities markets have led to limited increases in producer and consumer prices, but there is no reason to fear this will result in a broadening of inflationary trends.
German economy still in uptrend - Econ Ministry

The ministry repeated its prediction that the number of unemployed would decline in spring more rapidly than the seasonal norm, as special factors that drove it higher at the beginning of the year fall away.

The flattening of economic growth in the fourth quarter after two strong preceding quarters was not a sign of renewed weakness, but was entirely due to extraordinary factors including a high number of "bridgeable" holidays, the ministry said in its regular monthly report for March.
"Recent developments give no grounds for a correction of the (projected) real growth rate of 2.5 percent on which the government's annual report on the economy is based," it said.
The report, which was issued in January, already took into account the flattening of growth in the fourth quarter.
Upward forces such as low interest rates, stable prices, the stabilisation of the mark against the dollar and a dynamic world economy will rapidly regain the upper hand, it said.

"The price climate in Germany remains unusually favourable," the report said. "Room for domestic price increases remains limited, and unit wage costs, the most important domestic cost component, are retreating.
Producer prices in January were only 0.7 percent higher than a year earlier, while construction prices have been falling for a long time.
